datasets.name: Most Streamed Spotify Songs 2024
datasets.description: About 4,600 of the most streamed songs of 2024, with streaming, playlist, video and radio numbers from more than a dozen platforms.
datasets.author: Nidula Elgiriyewithana
datasets.changes: Modified from the original CSV: converted to a SQLite table named songs, text decoded as Windows-1252, numbers with thousands separators converted to real numbers, release dates converted to YYYY-MM-DD, the empty TIDAL Popularity column removed, and 2 rows with a repeated ISRC removed.
notes: Roughly 1 in 9 track, album or artist names lost their accented characters before this data reached us (for example Beyoncé appears as Beyoncï¿). That damage is in the original file and can't be repaired.
Many numeric columns have missing values, which show up as NULL. For example, almost half of the songs have no SiriusXM spins.

datasets.name: Palmer Penguins
datasets.description: Body measurements of 344 penguins of three species, recorded on three islands in the Palmer Archipelago, Antarctica, from 2007 to 2009.
datasets.author: Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station LTER; packaged by Allison Horst, Alison Hill and Kristen Gorman
datasets.changes: Converted from the CSV to a SQLite table named penguins, an id column added, and missing values (NA) stored as NULL.
notes: A few penguins have missing measurements or no recorded sex. Those show up as NULL.

datasets.name: Chinook music store
datasets.description: A digital media store: 275 artists, 347 albums, 3,503 tracks, 59 customers and 412 invoices, in 11 linked tables.
datasets.author: Luis Rocha (Chinook Database)
notes: The music catalogue comes from real iTunes libraries. The customers, employees and sales are made up, so treat them as realistic sample data.
Table and column names use PascalCase, such as Track and TrackId. SQL doesn't care about upper or lower case here.

datasets.name: NYC flights 2013
datasets.description: About 33,700 flights that left New York City in 2013 (every 10th flight), with airlines, airports, planes and hourly weather.
datasets.author: Hadley Wickham (nycflights13 package). Original data from the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics and other US government sources.
datasets.changes: Converted from CSV files (via the Rdatasets mirror) to SQLite tables. Missing values (NA) stored as NULL; the year and time_hour columns dropped; dewp, wind_dir, wind_gust and pressure dropped from weather; a flight_date column added to flights and a weather_date column to weather; only every 10th flight kept, to keep the download small.
notes: Times such as dep_time are stored as HHMM numbers (517 means 5:17 am), as in the original.
Cancelled flights have no departure time, so dep_time and dep_delay are NULL for them.

datasets.name: Titanic passenger manifest
datasets.description: 891 passengers from the Titanic's maiden voyage, with class, fare, family size and who survived.
datasets.author: Kaggle ("Titanic: Machine Learning from Disaster" competition)
datasets.changes: Converted from the CSV to a SQLite table named titanic, unchanged otherwise — empty cells stored as NULL.
notes: Age is missing for about 1 in 5 passengers, and Cabin for more than 3 in 4 — this is deliberately left as-is, not imputed.
Name embeds a title (Mr., Mrs., Master, Dr., ...) as free text — extracting it is a common first exercise, not a provided column.

datasets.name: Online Retail (UK, Dec 2010 – Feb 2011)
datasets.description: About 62,900 line items from a UK-based online gift retailer's invoices over a 2-month window.
datasets.author: Dr. Daqing Chen, UCI Machine Learning Repository
datasets.changes: Converted from the original Online Retail.xlsx to a SQLite table named online_retail, subset to invoices dated 2011-01-01 through 2011-02-28 (the full file covers all of Dec 2010 – Dec 2011 and is too large to bundle), empty cells stored as NULL. Nothing else altered.
notes: About 1 in 3 rows has no CustomerID — these are real anonymous or guest transactions, not a data error.
Cancelled orders are coded as an InvoiceNo starting with the letter C and have a negative Quantity — they are not flagged separately.
Description has a small number of non-product placeholder values (e.g. damaged stock, postage) mixed in with real product names.

datasets.name: Adult Census Income
datasets.description: 32,561 records from the 1994 US Census, used to predict whether someone earns over $50K a year.
datasets.author: Ronny Kohavi and Barry Becker, UCI Machine Learning Repository
datasets.changes: Converted from adult.data to a SQLite table named adult with an added header row (workclass, occupation, native_country, etc. — the original file has no header). Leading spaces trimmed from every field. Nothing else altered.
notes: Missing values are NOT stored as NULL here — the original data marks them with a literal "?" string, in workclass, occupation and native_country. That is deliberate: finding a disguised sentinel value is part of the point.

datasets.name: Student Performance (Math & Portuguese)
datasets.description: Survey and grade data for 395 math students and 649 Portuguese-language students at two Portuguese secondary schools.
datasets.author: Paulo Cortez, UCI Machine Learning Repository
datasets.changes: Converted from student-mat.csv and student-por.csv (semicolon-delimited) to two SQLite tables, student_math and student_portuguese, in the same database. Nothing else altered.
notes: Some students appear in both tables (same student, two subjects) — there is no shared key provided to match them.
G1, G2 and G3 are period grades on a 0-20 scale, not a percentage.
Several columns (Dalc, Walc, famrel, health, ...) are 1-5 Likert-style ratings mixed in with yes/no fields and true 0-20 grades — they look alike as plain integers but mean very different things.

datasets.name: World Development Indicators (5 series, 2003–2023)
datasets.description: GDP per capita, life expectancy, population, CO2 emissions per capita and the extreme poverty rate, for ~215 countries and regions, 2003–2023.
datasets.author: The World Bank

source.name: World Bank Open Data (World Development Indicators)

datasets.changes: Downloaded 5 indicators separately (NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, SP.DYN.LE00.IN, SP.POP.TOTL, EN.ATM.CO2E.PC, SI.POV.DDAY) from the World Bank API, reshaped from their original wide (one column per year) format to one row per country/year, merged into a single world_dev_indicators table, and trimmed to 2003-2023. Empty cells stored as NULL. Nothing else altered.
notes: The country column mixes real countries with regional and income-group aggregates the World Bank reports the same way (e.g. "World", "Sub-Saharan Africa", "Arab World") — nothing here filters those out.
Coverage varies a lot by indicator: the poverty rate in particular is only reported for a fraction of country-years.
The CO2-emissions source file contained a small number of literal duplicate rows for the same country and year — these were kept exactly as published, not deduplicated.

datasets.name: NOAA Storm Events, 2023 (6 states)
datasets.description: 19,250 storm/weather events from 2023 in Texas, Oklahoma, California, Florida, North Dakota and Louisiana — type, damage estimates, casualties and a narrative for each.
datasets.author: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
datasets.changes: Downloaded the full 2023 StormEvents_details file, subset to 6 states and 19 of its 51 original columns, converted to a SQLite table named storm_events. Empty cells stored as NULL. Nothing else altered.
notes: DAMAGE_PROPERTY and DAMAGE_CROPS are text like "40.00K" or "2.00M", exactly as published — they are not parsed into numbers.
TOR_F_SCALE, BEGIN_LAT and BEGIN_LON only apply to certain event types (tornadoes, geocoded events), so most rows have them as NULL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE is free text written by NOAA staff, varying a lot in length and detail.

datasets.name: Airbnb listings — Asheville, NC
datasets.description: 2,865 active and inactive Airbnb listings in Asheville, North Carolina, from a September 2026 snapshot.
datasets.author: Inside Airbnb
datasets.changes: Converted from the 2026-09-19 listings.csv snapshot to a SQLite table named airbnb_listings, trimmed from 90 original columns to 22. Empty cells stored as NULL. Nothing else altered — price is kept exactly as published.
notes: price is text with a leading dollar sign (e.g. "$98.60"), not a number — about 1 in 10 listings has no price at all.
bathrooms_text is a free-text description (e.g. "1.5 baths", "Half-bath"), not a plain number.
A listing with no reviews yet has NULL for first_review, last_review and every review_scores_* column.

datasets.name: Open Food Facts — US products
datasets.description: 5,445 US food products with brand, category and nutrition facts, from the crowd-sourced Open Food Facts database.
datasets.author: Open Food Facts contributors
datasets.changes: Downloaded a prefix of the full product CSV export, filtered to products tagged United States with a non-empty product_name, flattened the per-product nutrient list down to 5 named nutrients per 100g, and sampled down to 5,445 rows (a mix of products with and without nutrition facts, not a random sample of the whole filtered set) for a SQLite table named openfoodfacts. Empty cells stored as NULL. Nothing else altered.
notes: This is crowd-sourced data: completeness (a 0-1 score) and last_modified_t (a Unix timestamp) reflect how much any one contributor filled in, not how important the product is.
nutriscore_grade is sometimes a real grade (a-e) and sometimes the literal text "unknown" or "not-applicable" — those are not missing values, they are what Open Food Facts itself recorded.
brands, categories and labels can each hold several comma-separated tags in one cell.
